Tap Stop to end the microphone session.
Enable notifications in Android Settings to stop the live microphone from the notification shade. You can always stop from the app.
Allow microphone access to send live sound to your audio output. You can grant access in Android Settings.
Couldn’t start. Open Instant Mic and try again.
Couldn’t start audio. Reconnect your output and try again.
Android couldn’t give Instant Mic audio access. Try again when other audio is idle.
Another app or call interrupted audio. Tap Start to try again.
Check that Android microphone access is on, then tap Start.
The microphone is unavailable. Check Android’s microphone access and close apps using it.
Android switched the microphone input. Disconnect the external microphone and try again.
Audio output changed. Check your connection or choose an output, then tap Start.
Couldn’t confirm the audio output. Check the connection and media audio in Android Settings.

Instant Mic accesses the microphone when you tap Start. It processes live audio in memory and plays it through Android’s active audio output, which can include a Bluetooth accessory you choose. Pair accessories in Android Settings.

Instant Mic saves no recordings, discards audio buffers when the session ends, and sends no data to servers. It has no accounts, ads, or analytics. Your preferences stay on this device until you clear app storage or uninstall.

Use Stop in the app or in the live notification when notifications are allowed. Manage permissions in Android Settings.

For privacy questions, use the developer email in the App support section of the Instant Mic listing on Google Play.
